dedupe_keys.name: first retrogressive thaw slump rts inventory for the kanin peninsula nw russia

description: First retrogressive thaw slump (RTS) inventory for the Kanin Peninsula (NW Russia) is a data set described in a peer-reviewed Scientific Data article written by Ionut Cristi Nicu et al. Retrogressive thaw slumps (RTS) are thermokarst landforms resulting from the thawing of ice-rich permafrost in the pan-Arctic and high mountain regions, recognized as climate-related phenomena. Using 2022 ESRI Wayback satellite imagery, we manually digitized 900 RTS polygons on the Kanin Peninsula (NW Russia), categorizing them into 633 inactive and 267 active features based on morphology and vegetation patterns. Coverage: national (RU); published in 2025. Formats: Shapefile. The data are held in Zenodo and reached through its DOI listed on this page; the paper's Data Records section names it. Access is free of charge and open according to the article. The licence is CC-BY-4.0, taken from DataCite rights of the deposit. Caveats: written from the Scientific Data article metadata (title, abstract, Data Records section) read on 2026-10-01; the data themselves were not opened or downloaded, so their contents, quality and current availability were not checked. It can support transport-network, traffic and mobility studies. Related records: none catalogued yet.
